summary: Frontend-only Playwright regression on the NEW real-geography India map (IndiaMap.jsx + indiaMapPaths.json). All 34 mainland regions + 2 island insets are present, 36 chips render with FULL names (no abbreviations), no old duplicate UTs (DD/DH removed), Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu is one merged UT (id=DN), and Jammu & Kashmir (JK) and Ladakh (LA) are separate. SVG is real geography (WB path d = 841 chars, viewBox 0 0 100 110, no <text> nodes inside SVG). 11 of 12 required region clicks open the correct DetailPanel with the right name + capital. Only Puducherry (PY) map-region click routes to Tamil Nadu (PY chip works fine). Tooltip on hover, mark-as-learned (map region colour, chip colour, stat-india, persistence across refresh), practice-capital -> India Quiz, chip -> map 'selected' highlight all PASS. Regression sweep (Explorer Grid search+UT filter, National Symbols, World Explorer, Passport, mobile 390 overflow) all PASS. Passport 'Maximum update depth exceeded' bug from iteration 1 is FIXED (0 errors observed). 0 console errors during full navigation.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking the PY <path> element (data-testid=map-region-PY) opens the Tamil Nadu DetailPanel instead of Puducherry. Root cause: Puducherry consists of 4 tiny disconnected enclaves (Puducherry, Karaikal, Yanam, Mahé). The combined SVG path's bounding-box CENTRE falls in TN territory / ocean, not on any PY-painted pixel. Playwright's default .click() lands at BBox centre and therefore hits the TN path underneath. Users clicking directly on visible PY pixels (small dots along the east coast) should still open PY because PY is rendered after TN in the DOM, but any interaction relying on BBox-centre (assistive tech, some automation) hits TN. The chip-PY button works correctly and opens Puducherry.

action_items: OPTIONAL FIX for PY click routing: Either (a) render Puducherry with an additional small pointer-events-boosting hitbox (a slightly-larger transparent circle or path around each of its 4 enclave centroids also carrying data-testid=map-region-PY so BBox-centre falls inside one of them); or (b) treat PY like AN/LD and move it to a small inset button below the SVG so it is always reliably clickable; or (c) keep as-is and rely on chip-PY for reliable access (already works). No other action items — everything else in the map replacement is working correctly.

rca of the issue: PY map-region click routing to TN: The <path d> for Puducherry is a compound MULTIPOLYGON of 4 tiny non-contiguous enclaves along India's east coast. Its SVG bounding box therefore stretches across a mostly-empty rectangle whose CENTRE is not inside any painted PY pixel — it falls on Tamil Nadu's fill or in the sea. Playwright's default click strategy computes element bounding-box, moves to centre, and clicks; the click therefore lands on the TN path (which is behind PY in DOM order but visible at that pixel because PY has no fill there). Fix options: (1) split PY into 4 sibling <path> elements each with data-testid=map-region-PY (would then click on any enclave); (2) add invisible larger circular hitboxes around each PY centroid; or (3) demote PY to the inset-button row alongside AN/LD (cleanest UX for a UT with tiny scattered enclaves). Real end-users can still click on the visible PY dots because DOM order paints PY on top of TN there, but the failure mode above will bite anyone using automation, screen-reader default focus, or clicking near-but-not-exactly on the tiny visible dots.
